reviews.comment: This was the worst of all the professor options for this class in my opinion. His class was unnecessarily confusing, and it felt like the professor made simple topics harder than they had to be. They also did not provide as many resources or as much help as the other professors. Overall, not a good teacher. He rambles a lot as well.

Very funny guy but his lectures are kinda disorganized. Quizzes are take-home, which is nice. Best thing about his class was he recorded every lecture on zoom, so I maybe showed up to 2 total classes all semester. Tests are pretty difficult, averages were mid-70s. HWs and quizzes not difficult at all, just make sure you know your stuff for tests

Poorly structured lectures, unclear materials, and dismissive responses to student concerns. When I asked for support, I was always given unclear answers despite putting in real effort. This class felt more like surviving confusion than learning fluid mechanics. Worst professor I have ever had. Had to pull multiple (6+) all nighters to pass.
I didn't attend class regularly and probably went to

Dr. Felts is a great guy and good lecturer. Classes were fun and useful, but often veered off topic. Exams were difficult in the 50 min time frame. Many homeworks were fine, but some were horrible and not helpful at all. Definitely get the textbook!

Professor Felts was a great choice for Heat Transfer.  He was a great lecturer and very knowledgeable.  His lectures were funny and enjoyable.  The exams were difficult, but fair.  You will have to work for an A in this course, but it is doable.  I would definitely recommend taking Professor Felts if you really want to learn the material.

Often went off-topic in lectures. Had no lecture notes posted and in-class notes were hard to follow. Exams were very different to the homework and quizzes. Was very late to office hours if he showed up at all. Take someone else for heat transfer
Didn't stay on topic during lectures. No lecture notes were posted. Exams were not similar to hw/quizzes. Always late to office hours. I would recommend taking someone else.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Felts is probably one of the best heat transfer professors you can take at A&M. Felt's lectures were clear and organized while helping answer students' questions. Dr. Felts was lenient on grading criteria for homework and exams. All of the exams are open book and open notes, but you should still know concepts. I highly recommend to get him.

You will learn heat transfer very well in Felts' class. He goes above and beyond to teach you about things you may see in industry related to heat transfer. Notes are very clear, broadcasts every class on zoom, tests are open internet, but you need to study to do well. Large MATLAB group project near the end of the semester. Take him if you can

Dr. Felts is one of the best professors I have had. He gives lectures basically from the textbook but still manages to make them interesting. If you pay attention during lecture the course material comes naturally to you. The homework, quizzes, and tests helped a lot with understanding heat transfer.

Tests were long, and that made them challenging at times, but he's a great professor. Best option for Heat Transfer if you want to actually learn it. Great guy. Super helpful on the group project if you go to his office. Curved each exam and made the final optional. Made class enjoyable.
Story time: he didn't tell us that his first test had no numbers. Cool guy, would totally take him out for a beer, but not as a prof.

Dr. Felts was a great teacher for fluids. All lectures are handwritten on the whiteboard. He is very knowledgable and eager to help you learn. Tests were sometimes hard but he made up for harder tests with an easier final. Take him if you really want to learn and understand fluids. The class wasn't easy but he is professor I would take again.
